title: Fixed wiring summaries and signed spectra leave different input counts in two selected Allen mouse circuit models
abstract: We tested dedicated-input control in equal signed linear models of 247 selected mouse and 17 selected human Allen slice circuits. Exact enumeration fixed each cell degree, class edge totals, two unsigned three-cell counts, reciprocal class counts and the signed characteristic polynomial. Nine mouse sets and one human set had several allowed wirings. The minimum independent input count changed between two and three in two mouse sets and in no human set. Single-cell reachable ranks changed in three mouse sets. Independent arithmetic and exhaustive four-cell checks passed. This is a conditional model counterexample, not a measured brain control result. Small samples, tied weights, omitted cells and slice detection limit biological use. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External record tables are not bundled.

display.caption: Finite audit counts under fixed cell degrees, class totals, tested motif counts and exact signed spectrum. No population inference is made.
